title: Finance & Legal: Integrated Budgeting, Procurement, Contracts, and RevRec Playbook (2026)
author: Aisha Patel
summary: This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference's end-to-end finance and legal operating procedures for budgeting & forecasting, procurement, contract review/approval, and revenue recognition & billing. It codifies approval thresholds, owners, operational SLAs, and links to templates and systems to ensure consistent, audit-ready execution.
scope: Applies to all Redwood business units and departments globally. Covers annual and rolling forecasts, capital and operating spend requests, vendor procurement and onboarding, contract lifecycle (negotiation through execution), and revenue recognition and billing practices for hosted, dedicated, and private offerings.
owners_and_contacts: Primary owners: FP&A (Budgeting & Forecasting) - FP&A Manager (fpna@redwood.ai), Procurement - Procurement Lead (procurement@redwood.ai), Legal - Senior Counsel (legal@redwood.ai), RevOps - Revenue Operations Manager (revops@redwood.ai). Escalation path: Department Head -> VP Finance -> CFO.
budgeting_process_overview: Quarterly and annual budgeting is coordinated by FP&A. The cadence is: 1) Planning kick-off (T-12 weeks) with target guidance from Finance; 2) Department submissions (T-8 weeks) including headcount, OPEX, and CAPEX; 3) Cross-functional review and scenario modeling (T-6 to T-4 weeks); 4) Leadership review and approval (T-2 weeks); 5) Board/CEO sign-off. Departments must submit standardized budget templates located at /confluence/finance-and-legal/budget-templates. All budget items must map to a cost center and GL code.
forecasting_process: Rolling-forecast cadence: monthly 12-month rolling forecast with a deeper quarterly reforecast. Key inputs: booking cadence from SalesOps, committed spend from Procurement, headcount changes from People Ops. FP&A maintains a forecast variance dashboard (target: forecast accuracy > 95% for consolidated ARR within +/- 3% quarterly). Forecast owners must annotate material variance (>5% by line) with root cause and remediation plan.
approval_matrix_table:
| Amount | Required Approvals | Documentation Required |
|-------:|-------------------|-----------------------|
| <$5,000 | Requesting Manager | Expense request, justification |
| $5,000 - $50,000 | Manager + Finance Reviewer | Vendor quote(s), SOW/estimate, procurement form |
| $50,000 - $250,000 | Director + Procurement Lead + Finance | Two quotes or vendor selection memo, SOW, risk assessment |
| >$250,000 | VP Finance + Legal + CEO sign-off (if strategic) | RFP/selection memo, signed contract template, security & privacy review |
procurement_procedures: Procurement follows the vendor lifecycle: 1) Need identification and business justification; 2) Vendor discovery and preferred vendor check; 3) Request for Quote (RFQ) or RFP for purchases >= $50k; 4) Commercial terms negotiation (Procurement and Legal); 5) Security and privacy review (Security team) for vendors handling customer data; 6) Purchase Order (PO) issuance via Coupa (or configured procurement system) before work begins; 7) Invoice validation and three-way match: PO, goods/service confirmation, invoice. Preferred payment terms: Net 30 unless otherwise approved. Vendor onboarding checklist: signed W-9/COI, security questionnaire, KYC for >$100k cumulative spend.
vendor_onboarding_steps: 1) Complete Vendor Intake Form (procurement system). 2) Legal attaches master services agreement (MSA) or selects appropriate template. 3) Security performs vendor risk assessment (high/medium/low). 4) Procurement issues PO after approvals. 5) Finance sets up vendor in AP system and maps cost center. Target SLA: vendor onboarding completed within 10 business days for standard vendors; 20 business days for high-risk vendors requiring remediations.
contracts_process_and_requirements: Contract lifecycle steps: 1) Request initiation (Sales/Engineering/Partnerships) with commercial terms; 2) Legal drafts or reviews the appropriate template (MSA, SOW, NDA); 3) Risk classification (standard, negotiated, high-risk). Approval thresholds: Legal review required for any contract > $50,000 or containing non-standard IP/data/indemnity clauses. For customer contracts: Revenue Ops must confirm pricing and billing schedule. For reseller/partner agreements: Partnerships and Legal co-own negotiation. Contract signing: use DocuSign and ensure executed copy is uploaded to Contract Repository (link: /confluence/finance-and-legal/contracts-repository).
contract_review_checklist:
- Confirm commercial terms (term length, termination, renewal, pricing).
- Verify scope of work and acceptance criteria.
- Confirm data residency, security, and privacy clauses.
- Review IP and indemnity clauses; flag non-standard requests.
- Confirm insurance requirements and proof (COI).
- Ensure billing and payment terms mapped to RevOps schedule.
- Escalate any legal exceptions to Senior Counsel.
revenue_recognition_policy_summary: Revenue recognition follows ASC 606 principles. Revenue is recognized when performance obligations are satisfied. Standard revenue streams: Hosted API (usage-based), Dedicated (capacity/commit), Private (license + services), Professional services (one-time). Billing cadence and recognition rules: 1) Usage-based hosted API: invoiced monthly and recognized in same period as the usage (deferred revenue immaterial if invoiced mid-month). 2) Dedicated commitments: upfront payments are allocated across the committed term and recognized ratably. 3) Private deployments and professional services: recognize according to milestone completion or percent-complete (if measurable and reliable). Revenue deferral and breaking changes require RevOps + Accounting sign-off. All recognition judgments must be documented in RevRec worksheet stored in /confluence/finance-and-legal/revrec-and-billing/.
billing_and_invoicing_procedures: Billing system: Stripe for hosted/marketplace; Netsuite/BillingSuite for enterprise invoicing (integrated with Salesforce). Invoicing SLA: issue invoices within 5 business days of period close for usage invoices, and within 3 business days of milestone acceptance for services. Collections SLA: initial invoice sent at T+0, reminder at T+15 days, escalation to AR Manager at T+30 days, and legal collections at T+60 days for unpaid net-30 invoices. Credits/adjustments require RevOps approval and Finance reconciliation. Dispute handling: Sales Owner opens a dispute ticket in Zendesk Tickets for Billing; RevOps investigates and resolves within 10 business days.
internal_controls_and_audit_requirements: Key controls: PO required before contract execution where applicable, segregation of duties (requester/approver/payer separation), two-person approval for spend >$250k, monthly GL reconciliations by Finance, and quarterly internal control self-assessment. Audit evidence: signed contracts, POs, invoices, payment confirmations, vendor due diligence files, and approval emails stored in DocStore/SharePoint. External audit timeline: provide annual audit package by May 15. Internal control KPIs: % of PO-backed spend (goal > 95%), invoice match rate (goal > 98%), and days sales outstanding (DSO) target < 45 days.
escalation_and_exception_process: Exceptions to this playbook must be documented and approved: 1) Submit Exception Request Form to FinanceOps and Legal. 2) Exception reviewed within 3 business days; high-risk exceptions escalated to VP Finance and GC. 3) Approved exceptions are recorded in the Risk & Exceptions register with owner and remediation deadline. Examples: fast procurements for engineering incident response, one-off contract amendments under $25k where time-to-market justifies deviation.
templates_and_artefacts: Location of standard artifacts: Budget templates - /confluence/finance-and-legal/budget-templates; Contract templates (MSA, SOW, NDA) - /confluence/finance-and-legal/contract-templates; Vendor intake & PO form - Procurement system; RevRec worksheets - /confluence/finance-and-legal/revrec-and-billing/. Use the canonical templates; any template deviation requires Legal sign-off.
monitoring_and_reporting: Finance publishes a monthly Financial Pack: P&L by product, Cash forecast (90-day), Balance sheet variances, and RevRec movements. Procurement publishes a quarterly vendor spend report and vendor risk heatmap. Ownership: FP&A produces the Financial Pack; RevOps produces the revenue and MRR movements report. KPI dashboard (internal) tracks forecast accuracy, DSO, PO coverage, and vendor onboarding SLA.
training_and_comms: Onboarding & annual refresh training required for all hiring managers and procurement requesters. Finance runs quarterly office hours for budget owners. Major policy changes communicated via all-hands and documented change log in this page's history. Training artifacts and recordings stored at /confluence/finance-and-legal/training/.
